title: Fire in the hole! (With Slate)
description: Walking through the woods can be a blast for some - for others it can lead to a dangerous discovery. Airman First Class Jay Brackins joins the dirt boys and 18th Civil Engineer Squadron at Kadena as they carry out an explosive mission.
keywords: uxo, munitions, Dirt Boys, C4, 18th CES, AIr Force, people, operations, Okinawa, Japan, 18th Wing, explosive ordnance disposal, Ordnance, military

transcript.text: - [Narrator] Members from Kadena's
Explosive Ordinance Disposal or EOD team
start their morning with a bang.
As they prepare for a controlled detonation.
- We had 12 rocket motors and 64
smoke grenades that we got rid of today
and also two legacy UXO's that we collected here
on the island through our own emergency responses.
- [Narrator] Sometimes munitions are shipped to the states
and can cost up to--
- [Soldier] Like 11.2 million to gen up an entire ship
full of explosives to go back so if we can reduce that load
and alleviate some of that cost that's a good impact.
- [Narrator] Not only is it fiscally beneficial,
it's also good for training other members of the team.
- They get to do a demolition
that they wouldn't get a chance to do otherwise,
they get to practice the protective works.
Like you saw here today where we were
burying our shot to contain the fragmentation.
To me that's one of the biggest benefits.
But coming out here and doing this kind of work
where we actually get to do the explosive work
is the reason why we all do this.
- [Narrator] You can start your morning
with a shot of espresso but EOD starts their morning
with something a little more high energy.
Airmen 1st class Jay Brackins.
- [Man] Fire in the hole.
(bang)
- [Narrator] Kadena Air Base Japan.
